headline: Foundation repair in Baton Rouge.
intro: Cracked brick, sticking doors, sloping floors and slabs that have moved. We look at what is happening, explain why, and tell you what it will take to fix it.
sectionHeadline: Baton Rouge soil swells when it is wet and shrinks when it is dry.
about: Most of the ground around Baton Rouge is clay. After weeks of rain it swells and lifts; after a dry summer it shrinks and drops away from the slab. Do that for twenty or thirty years and a house moves. Local Pro Foundation Repair starts with a look at the whole picture — the cracks, the floors, the drainage and the trees — so the fix matches the actual cause, and you are not paying for piers when a gutter would have done it.

faqs.q: Is every crack a foundation problem?
faqs.a: No. Concrete shrinks as it cures, so thin hairline cracks in a slab are normal. Cracks that are getting wider, cracks wider than a coin's edge, stair-step cracks in brick, and cracks with one side higher than the other are the ones worth having looked at.

faqs.q: What are the signs of foundation trouble?
faqs.a: Doors that stick or will not latch, windows that bind, gaps between the wall and the ceiling or over the kitchen cabinets, floors that slope, and cracks in brick or drywall that run out from the corners of doors and windows.

faqs.q: Why do Baton Rouge foundations move?
faqs.a: Mostly clay soil and water. Clay swells when wet and shrinks when dry, and Baton Rouge swings between both. Poor drainage, big trees close to the house, and plumbing leaks under the slab make it worse.

A walk around the outside and inside of the house, floor-elevation readings, a look at drainage and nearby trees, and a crawlspace check on raised homes. Then an explanation of what we found and what we would recommend.

faqs.q: Do I need to move out during repairs?
faqs.a: Usually not. Most slab piering is done from the outside, and pier and beam work happens in the crawlspace. You may hear and feel some of it while the house is lifted.

faqs.q: Will repair fix the cracks in my walls?
faqs.a: Lifting the house often closes cracks partway, and doors frequently start working again. Cosmetic patching of drywall and brick is usually done after the house has been stabilized.

pages.heading: Slab foundation repair in Baton Rouge.
pages.intro: When part of a slab settles, piers driven down to firmer soil lift that section back and hold it there.
pages.seoTitle: Slab Foundation Repair Baton Rouge LA | Local Pro Foundation
pages.seoDescription: Slab foundation repair with steel and concrete piers in Baton Rouge, Central, Prairieville and Denham Springs. Inspections and leveling.

sections.heading: Dig, drive, lift, hold.
sections.body: Holes are dug along the beam where the slab has dropped. Piers are driven down until they reach soil that will hold, then jacks lift the slab back toward level and it is set on the piers. The holes are backfilled when the work is done.

sections.heading: Two common pier types.
sections.body: Pressed concrete pilings are stacked cylinders pushed into the ground under the weight of the house. Steel push piers go deeper, which matters where firm soil is far down. Which one fits depends on the house and the soil, and we will explain why we recommend one over the other.

sections.heading: Check the pipes under the slab.
sections.body: A leaking drain line under a slab can wash out soil and cause settling. Lifting can also stress old pipes. A plumbing test before or after repair is often a good idea, and we will tell you if we think it is needed.

faqs.q: Does the whole house need piers?
faqs.a: Rarely. Most repairs are on the section that has settled, often one corner or one side.

pages.heading: Pier and beam foundation repair in Baton Rouge.
pages.intro: Raised houses move differently from slabs. Piers sink or lean, shims rot or slip, and sills and beams soften where water gets in.
pages.seoTitle: Pier & Beam Foundation Repair Baton Rouge | Local Pro Foundation
pages.seoDescription: Pier and beam repair for raised homes in Baton Rouge: new piers, shims, sill and beam repair, and re-leveling of sagging floors.

sections.heading: Bouncy floors and soft spots.
sections.body: A floor that dips in the middle of a room, bounces when you walk or slopes toward one wall usually means a pier has settled, a shim has failed, or a beam or joist has rotted. The crawlspace tells the story.

sections.heading: Support, replace and re-shim.
sections.body: Settled piers are reset or new ones added, failed shims are replaced with steel, and damaged sills, beams or joists are repaired or sistered. Then the house is brought back toward level.

sections.heading: Keep the crawlspace dry.
sections.body: Standing water and humidity under a raised Baton Rouge house rot wood and invite termites. Vents, a vapor barrier and drainage away from the house protect the repair.

pages.heading: House leveling in Baton Rouge.
pages.intro: Sloping floors, sticking doors and gaps over the cabinets usually mean part of the house has dropped. Leveling brings it back.
pages.seoTitle: House Leveling Baton Rouge LA | Local Pro Foundation Repair
pages.seoDescription: House leveling for slab and raised homes in Baton Rouge, Central, Zachary and Denham Springs. Fix sloping floors and sticking doors.

sections.heading: Floor readings show where it dropped.
sections.body: We take elevation readings across the house to map the high and low spots. That shows which part moved and how much, and it is how we tell you what a repair is likely to accomplish.

sections.heading: Toward level, without breaking things.
sections.body: An older house that has been out of level for decades may not come back to perfectly flat without cracking finishes. The goal is to stabilize it and lift it as far as it will safely go.

sections.heading: Cracks, floors, doors, drainage and trees.
sections.body: The outside brick and slab edge, gutters and grading, trees near the house, interior cracks, doors and windows, and floor elevations. On raised houses, the crawlspace too.

sections.heading: Sometimes the answer is drainage.

pages.heading: Brick and wall cracks: what they mean.
pages.intro: Some cracks are cosmetic. Some are the house telling you a part of it has moved. Here is how to tell the difference.
pages.seoTitle: Brick & Wall Cracks Foundation Baton Rouge | Local Pro Foundation
pages.seoDescription: What stair-step brick cracks, drywall cracks and slab cracks mean for your foundation. Foundation repair in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

sections.heading: Stair-step cracks follow the mortar.
sections.body: A crack that climbs diagonally through the mortar joints, especially from the corner of a window or door, usually means one part of the wall has settled relative to the rest. A crack that goes straight through the bricks themselves is worth a look sooner.

sections.heading: Drywall cracks at the corners.
sections.body: Cracks running up from the corners of doors and windows, gaps where the wall meets the ceiling, and nail pops in a line are common signs of movement. One hairline crack in a hallway may be nothing.

sections.heading: Mark the ends with a pencil.
sections.body: Put a pencil mark and the date at each end of a crack. If it grows past the marks over a few months, the house is still moving and it is time to call.

pages.heading: Drainage and foundation problems in Baton Rouge.
pages.intro: Water against the slab is behind a lot of foundation movement. Getting it away from the house is the cheapest repair there is.
pages.seoTitle: Foundation Drainage Baton Rouge LA | Local Pro Foundation Repair
pages.seoDescription: Gutters, downspouts and grading to keep water away from your foundation in Baton Rouge. Prevent settling before it needs piers.

sections.heading: Downspouts that dump at the slab.
sections.body: A downspout that empties right at the foundation soaks the clay in one spot every storm. Extending it several feet out, or into a buried line, keeps that corner from swelling and shrinking more than the rest.

sections.heading: The ground should slope away.
sections.body: Over the years, flower beds get built up and soil settles until water runs toward the house. Regrading so the ground falls away from the slab keeps water from pooling against it.

sections.heading: Drought moves houses too.
sections.body: In a long dry summer, clay shrinks away from the slab. Steady watering around the foundation during droughts helps keep the soil from pulling back.
